title: Construction of a Wireless-Enabled Endoscopically Implantable Sensor for pH Monitoring with Zero-Bias Schottky Diode-based Receiver
protocol: Prepare the ISFET pH sensor mounted on a printed circuit board (PCB).
Trim the solderable contacts to no longer than 3 mm in length.
Solder a 15 mm section of FEP coated cable to the solderable electrodes.
Inspect the pH sensor-cable assembly under a microscope for open circuits and shorts.
Check the assembly with an open-short tester.
Clean the pH sensor assembly in an ultrasonic cleaner for 5 min at 70 °C in a 5% solution of flux remover in water.
Rinse the pH sensor assembly in technical grade isopropyl alcohol for at least 3 min.
Let the pH sensor assembly dry in an oven at 80 °C for 15 min.
Mix an appropriate amount of two-part epoxy for encapsulation, using a minimum of 2 mL.
Transfer the mixed epoxy to a 1 mL syringe with a 0.5 mm flat end needle.
Coat the soldering area of pH sensors with epoxy.
Make sure to coat the whole area of PCB electrodes and the exposed wire.
Let the epoxy cure at room or elevated temperature (80 °C max), for this study 50 °C was used.
Inspect the coated area under a microscope.
If any uncoated metal parts are exposed, repeat steps involving coating with epoxy until there are no visual signs of uncoated metal.
Trim the wires to the length and angle shown in Figure 2.
Coat the ends with solder to avoid fraying.
Place the PCB on a flat surface, components side up.
Apply solder paste to all exposed gold-plated pads.
Place passive and active components using tweezers according to the Table of Materials.
Heat the PCB with a hot air gun to 150 °C for 2 min.
Increase heat to 260 °C to solder the components.
Let the PCB cool to room temperature, do not move it during cooling.
Inspect the PCB under a microscope to verify correct placement and absence of shorts.
Repair any shorts or incorrect component placement with a soldering gun or hot air gun.
Solder 5 wires to the components as shown in Figure 4.
Connect the wires soldered to the connector of the programmer.
Program firmware to the microcontroller using the programming software.
Set the programmer to power the device at approximately 2.5 V.
De-solder the 5 wires after programming.
Place the PCB on a flat surface, component side up.
Solder the AWG38 copper antenna wire (length of 3 cm) to the designated area on the PCB.
Wrap the soldered antenna wire around the edge of the PCB.
Fix the antenna wire to the edge of the PCB with cyanoacrylate adhesive.
Solder two battery holders to the opposite part of the PCB, as shown in Figure 6.
Solder the pH sensor assembly to the terminals on the PCB, as shown in Figure 7.
Insert two AG1 batteries into the battery holders.
Prepare an appropriate amount of epoxy for encapsulation of the device according to step 1.8.
Encapsulate the device with the epoxy using a syringe with a needle.
Let the epoxy cure at room temperature or slightly elevated temperature (do not exceed 50 °C because of the presence of batteries).
Create a titanium wire hook according to Figure 9.
Attach the wire hook to the device with a drop of fast-curing epoxy.
Let the epoxy cure at room temperature or slightly elevated temperature (50 °C maximum).
Proceed with step 3 while waiting for the sensor activation which occurs 24 hours after battery insertion.
Place the PCB on a flat surface.
Solder the components using the solder paste method described in steps 2.2-2.6 or use a soldering gun according to Figure 11A.
Inspect the PCB under a microscope.
Fix any shorts or incorrect component placement observed during inspection.
Attach an SMA connector to the PCB.
Attach a vector network analyzer input to the SMA connector.
Record the S11 Smith chart of the rectenna from 300-500 MHz with 1 kHz resolution bandwidth.
Observe the response and record the impedance at 431.7 MHz.
Use an impedance matching calculator software to determine the values of matching components.
Solder the impedance matching components.
Inspect under a microscope for short circuits and component placement.
Measure with spectrum analyzer again.
Confirm that the voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) is under 3 between 300-500 MHz.
If not, either repeat with different matching components or continue with the reduced performance of the rectenna in mind.
Connect the 433 MHz band antenna to the SMA connector.
Connect an oscilloscope to the rectenna output.
Set the oscilloscope to single-channel operation.
Set the oscilloscope to rolling time base.
Set the oscilloscope to DC mode.
Set the oscilloscope to 500 ms/div time base.
Set the oscilloscope to 5 mV/div voltage scale.
Study the material safety data sheets of the chemicals beforehand.
Use proper protective equipment when manipulating chemicals.
Prepare a 2% hydrochloric acid solution.
Prepare 100 mM buffer solutions of pH 4, pH 7, and pH 10 using standard laboratory procedures.
Mark the beakers containing the buffer solutions.
Verify the pH of all four beakers using a calibrated pH meter.
Adjust the pH if needed.
Submerge the capsule in each beaker.
Record at least three samples from each beaker.
Measure the period between the second and third pulse for each sample.
Fill in the provided spreadsheet with the measured periods.
Determine the calibration coefficients for the pH sensor using the spreadsheet.
After calibration, measure the time between the second and third pulse again.
Input the new measurements into the spreadsheet to determine the pH of the solution.
Prepare an ex vivo endoscopic porcine model consisting of the stomach and a long segment of the esophagus.
Grasp the sensor externally with a hemostatic clip.
Insert the endoscope containing the sensor into the model in the standard way.
Position the clip with the sensor near the lower esophageal sphincter.
Rotate the endoscope against the esophageal wall.
Open the hemostatic clip.
Push the sensor toward the esophageal wall.
Close the hemostatic clip and release it.
The sensor will remain attached to the desired location on the esophageal wall.
Place the receiver within 10 cm of the implanted sensor.
Inject 50 mL of solutions with various pH values into the esophagus.
Retract the endoscope after each injection.
Read the value from the sensor no earlier than 30 seconds after injection.
Wash the esophagus with 100 mL of deionized water between injecting different pH solutions.
